result.instructions: Recalld is an AI memory system. Namespaces organize data; they are not access controls. Store/search use the resolved session default when namespace is omitted; by-ID operations use the record namespace. Supply namespace explicitly for reproducible workflows. Use recordAccess:false for evaluation or inspection. Reinforce only deliberate usefulness feedback. Inspect every batch item: legacy batch flags do not guarantee every item succeeded. Current duplicate scans are bounded and non-exhaustive; similarity is not proof of equivalence, so do not automatically delete close matches. Forget is logical removal, not backup erasure. Application contract 1 is supported; explicit contract 2 fails before work. Public v2 retries, exact-pair cursors and readiness are not enabled. Do not infer embedding-profile identity from matching dimensions.

tools.description: Store a new observation, fact, or piece of context as a memory. The system automatically generates an embedding for semantic search. Use tags to categorize (e.g., "topic/rust", "project/recalld"). Memories decay naturally over time unless reinforced. The memory is always stored, but the result may carry a `nearDuplicates` object listing existing memories at cosine similarity 0.85 or higher. Act on it rather than ignoring it: if the new memory restates one of them, call `forget_memory` on the id you just created, then either `reinforce_memory` on the existing memory (nothing new to say) or `store_memory` again with `supersedes` set to the existing id (the fact changed). Leave both only when they are genuinely distinct facts that happen to read alike. Pass `checkDuplicates: false` to skip the check during bulk ingestion.

checkDuplicates.description: Report existing memories that closely resemble this one (default: true). Never blocks the store; it only adds a `nearDuplicates` object to the result. Set false for bulk ingestion, where one similarity scan per memory is not worth paying.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

entities.description: Named entities (people, places, orgs, titles) mentioned in this memory. Used for search indexing and graph linking.

fullText.description: Detailed content. Removed as memory decays to ghost phase. Limit is 1048576 UTF-8 bytes (1 MiB).

namespace.description: Memory partition (omitted or null: configured session default, then "default")

parentId.description: UUID of an existing memory in the same namespace, linked as this memory's parent. The store fails if the target does not exist or is in a different namespace.

summary.description: Short description of the memory. Limit is 2000 UTF-8 bytes, which is 2000 ASCII characters but fewer for text containing em dashes, curly quotes, accents, or emoji (2-4 bytes each).

supersedes.description: UUID of an existing memory in the same namespace that this one replaces. Recall returns this memory in place of the old one. The store fails if the target does not exist or is in a different namespace.

topics.description: Topic keywords describing what the memory is about, e.g. ["rust", "cooking", "career"]

tools.name: store_memory
tools.title: Store Memory

tools.description: Store multiple memories in a single call. Each item has the same schema as store_memory. Returns an array of results, one per input memory. Saves round trips for bulk ingestion. Items are stored in order and each is indexed before the next is checked, so a result entry may carry a `nearDuplicates` object naming an earlier item of the same batch as well as pre-existing memories. The recovery is the same as for store_memory: forget the new id and either reinforce the existing memory or re-store it with `supersedes`. Set `checkDuplicates: false` on an item to skip its check.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

memories.description: Array of memories to store (max 100 per call)

checkDuplicates.description: Report existing memories that closely resemble this one (default: true). Never blocks the store; it only adds a `nearDuplicates` object to this item's result. Set false for bulk ingestion, where one similarity scan per memory is not worth paying.

entities.description: Named entities (people, places, orgs, titles) mentioned in this memory.

tools.name: store_memories
tools.title: Store Memories (Batch)

tools.description: Search for relevant memories using a natural language query. Returns memories ranked by semantic similarity combined with memory strength (well-reinforced memories rank higher). This is the primary way to retrieve context from the memory system. Use compact=true (the default) for token-efficient results containing only id, summary, fullText, entities, and topics. Set compact=false to include full metadata, graph edges, and neighbor context.

compact.description: If true (default), returns only id, summary, fullText, entities, and topics per memory for token efficiency. Set to false to include full metadata (tags, score, phase, strength, timestamps, related edges) and graph neighbor context.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

depth.description: Graph hops to include related memories (default: 0, max: 3)

emotions.description: Filter to memories with these emotional tones (e.g., 'happy', 'anxious')

entities.description: Filter to memories mentioning these entities (people, places, proper nouns)

namespace.description: Which namespace to search (omitted or null: configured session default, then "default")

recordAccess.description: False disables retrieval access writes and behavioral record caches. Omitted/true synchronously records legacy exposure before success.

tags.description: Only return memories with ALL of these tags

timeRangeEnd.description: Upper bound timestamp: either milliseconds since Unix epoch (integer) or ISO 8601 string (e.g. "2024-06-24T00:00:00Z"). Memories created at or before this time get a relevance boost.

timeRangeStart.description: Lower bound timestamp: either milliseconds since Unix epoch (integer) or ISO 8601 string (e.g. "2024-06-24T00:00:00Z"). Memories created at or after this time get a relevance boost.

topics.description: Filter to memories about these topics (e.g., 'adoption', 'cooking')

tools.name: recall_memories
tools.title: Recall Memories

tools.description: Retrieve a specific memory by its ID. This MCP fetch does not record access.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

namespace.description: Optional assertion of the record's namespace. Mismatch fails before effects; omitted uses the record scope, regardless of session default. Null is invalid.

recordAccess.description: False disables retrieval access writes and behavioral record caches. Omitted/true synchronously records legacy exposure before success.

tools.name: get_memory
tools.title: Get Memory

tools.description: Strengthen a memory that proved useful. Increases its stability so it decays more slowly. Use after retrieving and benefiting from a memory. Quality ratings: 1=forgot (weakens), 2=hard, 3=good (default), 4=easy (strongest reinforcement).

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

namespace.description: Optional assertion of the record's namespace. Mismatch fails before effects; omitted uses the record scope, regardless of session default. Null is invalid.

tools.name: reinforce_memory
tools.title: Reinforce Memory

tools.description: Delete a memory's content. The memory moves to the Tombstone phase: its summary, full text and tags are erased and it stops appearing in recall, but its record and its graph edges are kept so relationship chains stay intact, and its UUID is never reused. Tombstoned memories are never reclaimed by the decay sweep, so they persist for the life of the database. Use for incorrect, outdated or harmful information that must stop being recalled immediately. To correct a memory, prefer storing the correction with `supersedes`.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

id.description: Memory UUID to forget. The memory moves to the Tombstone phase; its graph edges are kept and its UUID is never reused.

namespace.description: Optional assertion of the record's namespace. Mismatch fails before effects; omitted uses the record scope, regardless of session default. Null is invalid.

tools.name: forget_memory
tools.title: Forget Memory

tools.description: Delete several memories in a single call. Each moves to the Tombstone phase exactly as forget_memory describes: content erased, record and graph edges kept, UUID never reused, never reclaimed by the decay sweep. Returns an array of results, one per input id, in the order given. A `deleted: false` result means the id was unknown or the memory had already been forgotten.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

ids.description: Memory UUIDs to forget. Each moves to the Tombstone phase; its graph edges are kept and its UUID is never reused.

tools.name: forget_memories
tools.title: Forget Memories (Batch)

tools.description: Find memories semantically similar to a specific existing memory, or sample a namespace for clusters of near-duplicate memories (up to 200 records and 11 vector candidates per source, including self when returned; not exhaustive). Two modes: "single" (default) requires an id and finds similar memories to it; "scan" uses the configured default namespace when omitted. Clusters are threshold-connected, not necessarily all-pairs matches.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

limit.description: Maximum results per source memory in "single" mode (default: 10, max: 100)

mode.description: Operation mode: "single" (default) finds memories similar to a given id; "scan" detects duplicate clusters across a namespace

namespace.description: Scan scope (omitted/null uses session default); in single mode an optional assertion against the source record namespace, checked before effects. Omit for record scope; null is invalid in single mode.

recordAccess.description: False disables retrieval access writes and behavioral record caches. Omitted/true synchronously records legacy exposure before success.

sameNamespace.description: Legacy selector (default: true). The current single-mode adapter always uses the source record namespace, including when false. Ignored in scan mode.

threshold.description: Similarity threshold for "scan" mode duplicate detection (0.0-1.0, default: 0.85)

tools.name: find_similar_memories
tools.title: Find Similar Memories

tools.description: Create a new memory namespace for organizing memories by domain or project; namespaces are not access controls. Each namespace has its own embedding space and decay configuration. You can set a custom decay rate multiplier to make memories in this namespace decay faster, slower, or not at all. Embedding dimensions are fixed after creation.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

decayRateMultiplier.description: Decay rate multiplier for this namespace. 1.0 = normal (default), 2.0 = 2x slower decay, 0.5 = 2x faster decay, 0.0 = decay disabled. Omit to inherit global setting.

embeddingDim.description: Integer 1-8192; null is invalid. Fixed after creation. Omission inherits the default namespace dimension (fallback 1536).

initialStability.description: Positive finite starting stability in days (omitted or null: 3.7145)

tools.name: create_namespace
tools.title: Create Namespace

tools.description: Destroy a namespace and everything in it: every memory, every graph edge touching one, its search index entries, and its vector file on disk. There is no undo and no backup. A namespace that still holds memories is refused unless you pass force: true. This is also the only operation that reclaims tombstones — memories deleted with forget_memory keep a record for the life of the database, and nothing else ever removes it. The 'default' namespace cannot be deleted.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

force.description: Delete the namespace even if it still holds memories. Without this, a non-empty namespace is refused. Forced deletion permanently destroys every memory in the namespace and removes its vector file from disk. There is no undo and no backup.

name.description: Namespace to delete. The 'default' namespace cannot be deleted.

tools.name: delete_namespace
tools.title: Delete Namespace

tools.description: Get statistics for a memory namespace: live memory count, phase breakdown (full/summary/ghost), permastore count, average strength, edge count, and vector storage size. Use this to check how many memories exist or monitor namespace health. `memoryCount` and every figure derived from it EXCLUDE deleted (tombstoned) memories, and always equal full + summary + ghost, so it agrees with list_memories and list_namespaces. Tombstoned records are reported separately as `tombstoneCount`: they hold no content, but nothing except delete_namespace ever reclaims them, so a namespace showing one memory where eleven were stored has ten of them.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

namespace.description: Namespace name to get stats for (omitted or null: configured session default, then "default")

tools.name: namespace_stats
tools.title: Namespace Stats

tools.description: List all memories in a namespace with pagination and optional filters. Unlike recall_memories, this does not require a search query or embedding lookup — it returns memories sorted by creation date (newest first). Use this for browsing, auditing, or enumerating memories when you don't have a specific search query.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

entities.description: Only return memories mentioning ALL of these entities

limit.description: Maximum results per page (default: 50, max: 200). A larger value is rejected, not clamped.

namespace.description: Which namespace to list from (omitted or null: configured session default, then "default")

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination (default: 0)

tags.description: Only return memories with ALL of these tags (AND semantics)

timeRangeEnd.description: Upper bound timestamp: either milliseconds since Unix epoch (integer) or ISO 8601 string. Only memories created at or before this time are returned.

timeRangeStart.description: Lower bound timestamp: either milliseconds since Unix epoch (integer) or ISO 8601 string. Only memories created at or after this time are returned.

tools.name: list_memories
tools.title: List Memories

tools.description: List every memory namespace with its ID, embedding dimensions, live memory count, and creation date. Call this first when you do not know which namespaces exist, before targeting one with list_memories, list_tags, or namespace_stats. Counts exclude deleted (tombstoned) memories.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

tools.name: list_namespaces
tools.title: List Namespaces

tools.description: List the tag vocabulary with per-label memory counts, most common first. Use this to discover what labels already exist before filtering list_memories or recall_memories, and before storing — so you reuse an existing tag instead of inventing a near-duplicate. Results come in four buckets: plain tags, plus the entity, topic, and emotion labels derived from those fields, returned without their prefixes so they can be passed straight back to store_memory or list_memories. Counts cover live memories only; deleted memories are excluded.

allNamespaces.description: Count across every namespace instead of one. Cannot be combined with an explicit namespace.

contractVersion.description: Application contract version. This server currently supports version 1 only.

limit.description: Maximum labels returned per bucket (default: 50, max: 500). Each bucket also reports its untruncated total.

namespace.description: Which namespace to count within (omitted or null: configured session default, then "default"). Reads that namespace's memory records, costing about one list_memories call.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.title: List Tags
